matchedFiveCourseDiagnostic.knownRegression: Mandarin fell from 99/A to 89/B because one lesson lost the required visible Hanzi and tone-marked-Pinyin pairing.

performance.implementation: A lightweight public Scion identity leaf keeps model constants on the landing path while the provider, compiler, grader, exporters, and workspace remain lazy. Compiler copy variants share the existing compiler-frame request instead of adding a new generation-time request.

landingChecks: Scion V0.16.62, Connected, and On-device are visible without exposing the internal model identifier.
The changelog tooltip renders all ten release claims and states that Gemma weights are unchanged and the adapter remains inactive.
The final workspace shows one Living Course Compiler status spine, 14/14 lesson kernels, 9/9 compiled materials, Grade A, the connected Agent, and one package ZIP action.

remainingGap.texture: The 90/A texture score still records repeated study-guide and slide-deck tails across 13 of 14 lessons. These are advisory signals rather than encoded package defects, but they identify the next compiler-quality lane.
remainingGap.adapter: The research adapter reduces inference burden but has not beaten the base model on held-out multi-domain quality, so it remains inactive.
remainingGap.validation: The deterministic 98/A score is encoded defect-conformance evidence, not proof of factual accuracy, classroom outcomes, or paid-model parity.

claimBoundary: V0.16.62 proves that the untouched public Gemma 4 E2B base plus the Scion compiler can complete a real 14-lesson browser generation and export a 117-entry package at 98/A under grader 1.10.23, with zero encoded P0/P1/P2 findings and zero export warnings. It does not prove that the research adapter improves quality, that every course will score 98/A, that the package has been independently fact-checked or classroom-validated, or that Scion beats a paid frontier model.
